clue.text: Review in a paper is flawed

indicators.note: something flawed is damaged or out of true, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's critique is said to be poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' reads as a noun in the surface, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to review something is to assess or evaluate it.

clue.text: Fashions suitable to be shown in commercials

indicators.note: something shown in a programme sits within it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ads are television or print commercials
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: Clothing styles that are fit for display in advertisements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like a noun about clothes; it is a verb meaning shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fashion something is to shape or modify it to fit.

clue.text: Quickly find some cash — balance nil!

parts.note: P stands for a penny, a small amount of money
the rest is the balance remaining
nil is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to raise money when the account stands at zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: presto directs a performer to play very fast, hence quickly.

clue.text: He is hostile, letting out Alsatians

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a hostile person, the noun

indicators.note: letting dogs out sets them loose to run about, so the letters are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: An aggressive man unleashes his guard dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsatians is the British name for German shepherd dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is by definition someone acting with hostility against another.

clue.text: Wounded? This will buck you up

definitions.meaning: taken literally, someone hit by a bullet in the upper limb
a boost or stimulus, originally an injection

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the literal one: a gunshot wound to the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a stimulus or boost that revives someone, from the image of an injection.

clue.text: It makes for a full retirement

definitions.text: It makes for a full retirement

parts.words: It makes for a full retirement
parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, and one goes to bed full after the evening meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work, but it means retiring for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The last meal of the day, eaten before bed, leaves one well fed at bedtime.

clue.text: A highly profitable practice!

parts.note: a business practice that earns excessively, as lending money at extortionate interest does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' might suggest a doctor's surgery; it is a habit of lending.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending money at exorbitant interest rates yields excessive profit for the lender.

clue.text: Snoops about tax for men serving in company

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to snoop is to pry, so snoops means pries
VAT is value added tax, a sales tax in Britain

explanation.surface: Nosy officials investigate tax affairs on behalf of employees in a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a business; it is a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates are the lowest-ranked soldiers, and a company is an army unit they serve in.

clue.text: Periods when students may collect in public

definitions.text: Periods when students may collect in public

parts.words: Periods when students may collect in public
parts.note: collect means gathering charity money from the public, not students gathering together

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, students hold annual charity fundraising weeks with stunts and street collections.
explanation.definitionFit: British university charity weeks, when students raise money with collecting tins and stunts.

clue.text: One way of saying one doesn't like it?

parts.note: a means one, the indefinite article
a version is one particular account or rendering of something

explanation.surface: A query about how to express dislike for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a thing disliked, not the dislike itself, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym-ish: an aversion is a strong dislike, also the object of it.

clue.text: Finding a remedy for smoking, perhaps

definitions.meaning: preserving fish or meat, one method being smoking

explanation.surface: Looking for a way to give up cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both healing a disease and preserving food by salting, drying or smoking.

clue.text: Acquire money and become more common

parts.note: to gain is to acquire
currency is money in circulation

explanation.surface: Getting rich and losing exclusivity at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the whole clue literally, but only the last three words define; the first two build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an idea or word that spreads into wide use is said to do this.

clue.text: All the players express mild disapproval, before taking it back

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of mild disapproval

indicators.note: back means the word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: A whole orchestra tuts in annoyance, then withdraws the remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link word; 'back' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: a passage marked this is played by the whole orchestra together.

clue.text: Anyway, it's where Customs may look

definitions.meaning: literally inside any suitcase customs officers open

explanation.surface: Regardless, border officials might search luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning regardless or anyhow; literally, inside any piece of luggage being searched.

clue.text: Over the hill?

parts.note: read literally, beyond the top of a hill; idiomatically, too old

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is past and 'hill' is a peak, so the literal reading matches the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for someone no longer at their best, past their prime, literally beyond the summit.

clue.text: Old fighters, ones with fiery tempers

definitions.meaning: Second World War British fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: Veteran boxers who are quick to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a famous WWII British fighter plane and a term for hot-tempered people.

clue.text: Frequently out of date

definitions.meaning: describes the word itself, which is archaic

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the answer as a word: it is an archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word meaning often, so it is both a synonym and itself antiquated.

clue.text: He'd put cryptic clues in the list

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: A man adds puzzle clues to a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' seems to describe the clues, but it signals the rearrangement of HED and CLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a timetable or programme is a list of planned events.

clue.text: Conductor has to take the consequences

definitions.meaning: literally, an orchestra conductor must turn towards the score and players
accept the results of one's actions

explanation.surface: A conductor must accept the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for accepting unpleasant results; literally what a conductor does facing the orchestra.

clue.text: Bill lifts telephone, showing concern

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the word so it reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: Bill picks up the phone, being considerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: caring means showing kindness and concern for others.

clue.text: Shut tin-opener in cupboard

parts.note: to close is to shut
the opener of the word tin is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: Put the can opener away in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin-opener' is read as the opening letter of 'tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, mainly American: a closet is a cupboard or small storage room.

clue.text: Rate reform more certain — official!

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, reshaping the letters

parts.note: surer means more sure, more certain

explanation.surface: A reform of the rates is surely more certain, says an official.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the person in charge of an organisation's funds is one of its officials.

clue.text: Pay out starting odds before the finish

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds on a horse when a race begins
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A bookmaker paying out on a race, from starting odds to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the British betting term for a horse's odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spend money is to pay it out.

clue.text: Too delicate to use loud abuse

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
to rail is to complain abusively

explanation.surface: Someone too sensitive to shout insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frail means weak and easily broken, overly delicate.

clue.text: Short-time employer of vermin catcher

parts.note: mo is a short time, a moment
a user employs something, so is its employer

explanation.surface: A temporary boss hires someone to deal with rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-time' suggests reduced working hours; it is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cat that hunts mice is a catcher of vermin.

clue.text: What's inside is revealed by bird in nest-building

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
building puts the letters together in a new construction

parts.note: a rail is a type of wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird is seen building its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like part of the nature scene, but it signals rearranging the nest letters, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the internal organs, the innards of an animal.

clue.text: Second date broken by youth leader's girlfriend

indicators.note: broken means smashed up, so the letters are reordered
a leader comes first, so this takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A second date with a youth group leader's girlfriend goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns DATE into TEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang: a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend.

clue.text: Pupil power

parts.note: pupil is the eye's opening, not a schoolchild, and power is its ability

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil power' suggests student protest; the pupil is part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of vision, the eye's ability to see.
